questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The strong academic reputation of Imperial College London, the relevance of courses to my field, and the opportunity to gain international academic and professional experience in a leading research environment were the main factors

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The exchange was academically very rewarding, but also extremely demanding. The workload at Imperial is intense, and combined with the high cost of living in London, it sometimes felt difficult to fully enjoy the city or have much free time. However, I learned a lot, grew academically, and made close friends, especially among other exchange students. Overall, I am very grateful for the experience and the opportunities it provided

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a large amount of information shared via email, which at times could feel overwhelming and somewhat difficult to navigate. However, overall I felt well oriented once I arrived. The information was comprehensive, even if it required some effort to keep track of everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation programme that included a campus tour and meetings where we could ask questions, which was very helpful. The orientation took place about a week before courses started, giving enough time to settle in, get familiar with the campus, and organise practical matters. I did feel that there was relatively little information earlier in the process, but the support upon arrival itself was good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus housing was very challenging. As short-term exchange students are not eligible for university housing for stays shorter than a full academic year, I had to find accommodation privately in a very competitive and expensive market. I ended up paying around £2300 per month for four months, and it required significant effort to secure housing on relatively short notice. I would strongly recommend that future students begin their housing search as early as possible and explore multiple options well in advance.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Students should be aware that the private housing market in London is extremely expensive and fast-moving, and short-term rentals can be particularly difficult to secure. It is important to plan early and budget realistically for high living costs. In my case, I did not receive additional funding, so the financial commitment was significant. Being prepared for these challenges can help reduce stress when arriving.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Consider commute time carefully when choosing housing. Travel in London can easily take an hour or more, so proximity to campus or good transport links is very valuable.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before the semester, students receive a link where they can rank their course preferences (e.g. three priorities per slot). The allocation process worked smoothly, and it seemed likely to receive a first or second preference. After allocation, there is an opportunity to confirm or adjust selections if needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Administrative staff and course coordinators were available via email and provided guidance throughout the process. Information was communicated clearly, and it was possible to ask questions if anything was unclear.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was allocated my first preferences initially, but I later had to change one course because it could not be approved as a limited elective by my home university. Overall, the system allowed flexibility to adjust, which was helpful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check in advance which courses can be pre-approved by your home university, as this can affect your final choices even if you receive your preferred allocation. Rank your priorities carefully and have backup options, as some students may not receive their first choice. Planning ahead and confirming eligibility early can make the process much smoother.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level at Imperial is very high, as expected from a world-leading research university. The courses were intellectually stimulating and pushed me to develop strong independent learning skills. At times, the workload felt intense, but overall it was a valuable academic experience.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were academically demanding and required a high degree of independence. Much of the learning relied on self-directed reading beyond lectures, and students were expected to engage deeply with the literature. For “Advanced Topics” courses in particular, having a strong foundational background is important, as the material builds quickly on advanced concepts. There was also a significant amount of group work and presentations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more independent and research-oriented compared to UCPH. There was less structured guidance, and students were expected to take responsibility for identifying relevant reading and deepening their understanding outside of lectures. This encouraged critical thinking but could feel demanding, especially when adjusting to the expectations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Topics in Infection and Immunity
Advanced Topics in Parasitology and Vector Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the Advanced Topics courses for students who are interested in research and prepared for a challenging academic environment. They offer exposure to cutting-edge topics and encourage critical engagement with scientific literature. However, students should ensure they have sufficient background knowledge and be prepared for a significant workload.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Unexpected costs included higher-than-expected transport expenses, additional mobile data and SIM costs, and one-off setup costs such as purchasing household necessities (e.g. bedding, kitchen items). I also incurred visa-related fees (ETA), flights to travel home during the stay, and found that gym memberships (ca. 1000kr pr. month??) and everyday activities were significantly more expensive than anticipated. Overall, the cost of living in London was substantially higher than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and transport were significantly more expensive than expected, and food costs were also high. Social activities and general day-to-day expenses in London added up quickly. Items such as gym memberships and basic services were noticeably costly. Overall, most aspects of living expenses were higher than anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were various student societies, cultural events, sports clubs, and social activities organised through the university and student union. Regular events and opportunities to get involved were communicated via email and student platforms

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend exploring student societies and social events early in the semester, as they seem like good opportunities to meet people and build community. Getting involved early may help balance academic commitments with social life.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of being in London by exploring museums, parks, and different neighbourhoods, many of which are free to visit. I would also highly recommend exploring the food scene, as London offers a wide variety of authentic and diverse cuisines from all over the world. Trying different restaurants can be a great cultural experience, especially if your budget allows. It is also worth travelling to other parts of the UK or nearby countries, as London is very well connected.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting was relatively straightforward, as I had visited London before and was familiar with the general environment. However, living and studying there felt more intense than visiting, especially due to the fast pace and busy atmosphere of a large city. Over time I adapted, but I did miss the quieter environment of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Many local students already have established social groups, especially in later years, so it can require some initiative to connect. I found it helpful to engage through group work or shared academic activities, but I also formed strong friendships with other exchange students who were in a similar situation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The pace and intensity of daily life in London, including crowded public transport and a generally fast-moving environment, felt different from Copenhagen. The academic culture also placed strong emphasis on independence, which required adjustment.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the diversity of cultures and perspectives at the university, with many international students from different backgrounds. It was inspiring to be in such a global academic environment and to learn from leading researchers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for a very high academic workload and a strong expectation of independent study.

Plan finances carefully, as living costs in London are very high.

Start planning housing and course approval early to reduce stress.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exchange is academically and professionally very rewarding, especially due to the strong reputation of Imperial and exposure to world-leading research. However, students should be prepared for a demanding environment and a fast-paced city, and consider how they prefer to balance academic and social life.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to study at a world-leading institution, learn from renowned researchers, and gain valuable academic experience that will be beneficial for my future career. It was also rewarding to build friendships with other international students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing the high academic expectations alongside the practical and financial challenges of living in London, as well as adapting to a very busy and demanding environment.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall, the experience was academically enriching and will be valuable for my future career. While the pace and workload were demanding, the exchange provided significant personal and professional growth.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
